episodes.title: Meet the Adelaide Professor who put Australian physics on the map

stories.story: Adelaide Professor Anthony Thomas wins Prime Minister's Prize for Science
stories.angle: Celebrating the life and achievements of physicist Anthony Thomas and exploring the relationship between physics and artificial intelligence.
stories.voices: Sally Sara (host), Anthony Thomas (elder chair of physics at Adelaide University, pre-recorded interview). Anthony Thomas was given ample time to speak unchallenged.
stories.tone: Explanatory and congratulatory tone celebrating scientific achievement.
stories.emphasis: Foregrounded scientific contribution, basic science, and the evolving role of AI in physics research.
stories.evidence: mathematics is struggling at the moment because so many new results have come out of AI.

episodes.title: Changing Australia: Carly McKinnis and bringing and keeping more psychologists in regional Victoria

stories.story: Tackling the shortage of psychologists in regional and rural Australia
stories.angle: Addressing systemic shortages of mental health professionals in regional Victoria and innovative pathways to train and retain local psychologists.
stories.voices: Sally Sara (host), Carly McKinnis (clinical psychologist and co-founder and CEO of One Red Tree Resource Centre in Ararat, pre-recorded interview). Carly McKinnis was allowed to speak at length unchallenged.
stories.tone: Sympathetic, urgent, and focused on regional disadvantage.
stories.emphasis: Human impact of limited regional services, community-driven solutions, and the need for systemic support.
stories.evidence: we've been doing it in a little rural town in a way that's working without having to change pathways

episodes.title: 'Very rushed and an overreach' - Independent MP criticises new defence legislation

stories.story: Criticism of new federal defence security zone legislation
stories.angle: Independent and legal criticism of the federal government's rushed defence legislation granting sweeping powers to designate security zones.
stories.voices: Sally Sara (host), Andrew Wilkie (independent federal member for Clark in Tasmania, pre-recorded interview). Andrew Wilkie was given space to detail criticisms without interruption.
stories.tone: Critical and adversarial regarding government overreach.
stories.emphasis: Democratic accountability, potential misuse of extraordinary powers, and lack of adequate parliamentary scrutiny.
stories.evidence: it is an unreasonable extension of the power of the state.

episodes.title: Wells secures parliamentary support for digital safety laws

stories.story: Federal government secures Green support for digital safety duty of care laws
stories.angle: Balancing the regulation of tech platforms and legal remedies for online harm with free speech and censorship concerns.
stories.voices: Sally Sara (host), Anika Wells (Minister for Communications and Minister for Sport, pre-recorded interview), Andrew Hastie (Shadow Minister for Industry and Sovereign Capability, pre-recorded interview). Hosts challenged both guests on the implications of censorship and industry pushback.
stories.emphasis: Corporate accountability, international precedents, and potential impacts on free expression.
stories.evidence: this government is at the moment looking at redesigning psychology pathways in order to address this problem.
